question: Who is the administrator and custodian of fault domain R, and by what independent route do they authenticate?
evidence: 02 section 2 lists the required actual principal, administrators, substitute contracts and funding as deployment inputs and states that operational authority remains unavailable if they cannot be admitted. capabilities.json fulfillment_routes R-RUNTIME carries admission_state not_established.

packet.decision_required: Who is the administrator and custodian of fault domain R, and by what independent route do they authenticate?
packet.why_this_owner: The decision needs a named person who is not the founder acting as administrator A, an accepted custody arrangement and, if that person is paid, money. None of those is an agent's to supply. 02 section 2 states that the same person owning both accounts without independent accepted custody fails the claimed primary-admin-loss and owner-absence profile, so an agent choosing here would be choosing to void the architecture's central fault claim.
packet.latest_responsible_time: Before B10 operational admission, and before any operating promise that depends on recovery. B01 and B02 can build and test the witness protocol against local fixtures without it; 02 section 2 says local simulation cannot admit host or admin independence, so the need is real but not immediate.
options: Name a second natural person as custodian R with independent login, MFA and recovery, and record the compensation and availability window as an operating cost
Engage a professional custody or managed-recovery service under an accepted engagement with the same separation properties
Accept a single-custodian profile explicitly, which narrows the declared fault claim to exclude primary-admin loss and owner absence, and record that narrowing in 02 section 1
Defer operational admission until one of the above is available
consequences: A named independent custodian makes the zero-loss recovery objective testable at B10; it adds a recurring human cost and a second person who must be reachable within actual service deadlines
A service engagement converts the cost to a contract and introduces the provider as a new common root, which 02 section 2 requires to be recorded rather than assumed away
Accepting a single custodian is a coherent choice, but the architecture must then stop claiming survival of primary-and-backup loss; the claim, not the software, is what changes
Deferral leaves R-RUNTIME and R-REMEDY at admission_state not_established and blocks dependent promises
packet.uncertainty: Whether a suitable person or service exists within the founder's budget is unknown to this package; no candidate has been approached and no price has been obtained.
packet.reversibility: Reversible as a specification choice until infrastructure is purchased and data is placed. After real customer duties exist, changing custody is a migration with its own fencing and reconciliation.
packet.recommendation: No recommendation. This is a cost-versus-fault-tolerance trade-off that depends on the founder's risk tolerance and budget, both of which 03 section on operating setup reserves to the owner.
packet.if_no_answer: B01 through B09 proceed. B10 cannot complete, so no operating promise that depends on recovery may be made. This is recorded as an unavailable operating prerequisite, not as a narrowed plan.

Engage an external ombuds or professional complaints service under an accepted engagement
Do not make any offer available until one of the above exists, which keeps the grievance surface empty
consequences: A named funded recipient makes CAP-42's deadlines and escalation real and testable at B06
An external service supplies independence more cheaply than a second employee but adds a contract and a provider root that must be disclosed rather than called independent

Making no offer is the only honest alternative: 03 section on incidents says a reachable intake and a competent residual custodian must continue as long as required duties remain, so a sale creates this obligation whether or not the role is filled
packet.uncertainty: Response volume, and therefore the capacity this role needs, is unknown and will stay unknown until real customers exist.
packet.reversibility: Reversible before an offer exists. Once a duty has arisen, 03 section on incidents keeps the intake obligation alive after product closure, so the role cannot simply be withdrawn.

question: When a complaint names the custodian, who is the alternate recipient, who appoints them, and by when?
evidence: G-03's 'Honor rights under hostile noise' scenario, step 'Complaint names the custodian': the contracts catch the adverse variation and the report records 'Who the alternate is, who appoints, by when' as not specified. 03-company-capabilities.md CAP-42 and CAP-17.

packet.decision_required: When a complaint names the custodian, who is the alternate recipient, who appoints them, and by when?
packet.why_this_owner: CAP-17 routes such a complaint to an alternate and CAP-42 requires the recipient to sit outside the disputed decision and incentive dependency, but no document says who that alternate is or who has the standing to appoint them. Appointing the person who adjudicates a complaint against the founder's own custodian is a governance act; an agent selecting one would be selecting its own reviewer.
packet.latest_responsible_time: Before B10 admission and before the first offer, with Q-003. The G-03 scenario reached this step and found every other contract held, so this is the single unfilled role on that path.
options: Name a standing alternate in advance with an explicit appointing authority recorded in the AuthorityMatrix
Define an appointment rule — for example an external professional selected from a named panel — that resolves without the founder at the time of the complaint
Route such complaints to an external forum from the outset and record that forum's applicable scope
Leave it unfilled and accept that a complaint against the custodian has no admitted route
consequences: A standing alternate is testable at B06 and is the only option that survives founder absence
An appointment rule is weaker than a named person but stronger than nothing, and it is what CAP-41 already requires for succession: joint owner and provider loss must not depend on the absent owner
An external forum is independent by construction but has its own eligibility limits, which 03 says are the person's rights and a professional adjudication rather than this company's issuer limits
Leaving it unfilled makes CAP-42's independence promise false in the exact case it was written for
packet.uncertainty: Whether the applicable forum in the founder's jurisdiction accepts such a complaint, and on what terms, is a legal question this package does not answer and does not invent.
packet.reversibility: Reversible on paper. Not reversible once a complaint has been mishandled: 03 says a second native request ID is not another entitlement and the person's standing survives.
packet.recommendation: Recommendation: name a standing alternate AND record the appointing authority, because the two failure modes are different — an absent alternate and an alternate nobody may appoint.
packet.if_no_answer: The grievance route is admitted only for complaints that do not name the custodian, and that limitation is stated to the person rather than hidden. All other work proceeds.

packet.decision_required: Who is the independent assessor with write authority over protected-change acceptance, and what is their competence evidence?
packet.why_this_owner: 08 section 1 says that if independent competence is unavailable the protected change waits, and that the system does not invent a qualified proxy for the founder. That sentence makes the wait the founder's to resolve: the only way out is a real person with standing, and appointing one's own reviewer is precisely what the contract forbids the improver from doing.
packet.latest_responsible_time: Before the first ProtectedChange is authorized, which is B08. Every stage before B08 can be built, because construction under B00's frozen contracts is not itself a protected change.
options: Name an external reviewer with relevant competence under an accepted engagement, per protected subject
Name different assessors per subject family — authority and release, evidence and evaluation, recovery — since 08 section 1's registry already defines authority per subject
Accept that protected changes wait indefinitely, which is the specified behaviour and is safe but makes the system unimprovable
Reduce the protected-subject set, which is itself a protected change and so cannot be self-authorized
consequences: A named assessor makes B08's candidate-alters-the-gate tests meaningful; it costs money and calendar time per change and 06 section 8 requires that cost to be budgeted before the evaluation runs
Per-subject assessors match the registry but multiply the engagements
Indefinite waiting is the specified fail-safe. It means the system cannot fix itself, which 08 section 2 names as one of the conditions that falsifies the whole approach
Shrinking the protected set is the option most likely to be chosen for the wrong reason and is the one the architecture is built to make hard
packet.uncertainty: Whether relevant competence for these specific subjects is purchasable at all, and at what price, is unknown; the subjects are unusual and the assessor must be able to read the contracts.
packet.reversibility: Reversible: an assessor engagement can be ended and replaced. What is not reversible is a change activated without one, because 08 section 1 requires activation evidence that would then not exist.
packet.recommendation: No recommendation between the first two options. A recommendation against the fourth: reducing the protected set to escape the wait is the self-modification this register's RISK-15 exists to catch.
packet.if_no_answer: Protected changes accumulate as proposed and reviewed but never authorized. The system runs and does not improve. B01 through B07 and B09 proceed.

The founder asserts identity and a separate custodian holds the root key, which separates the two roles and interacts with Q-002
An external identity or custody service supplies the assertion, which introduces that service as a declared trust root
Leave the root unbound, which leaves the bootstrap predicates unsatisfiable in any real deployment

Separating the roles matches the A/R separation and needs the second person from Q-002

question: Who is the terminal owner of an unowned duty or harm, and does that party exist as a record?
evidence: Universal ownership and no ownership are one state [R5-11]. The national incident system defaults responsibility upward until delegated [R5-03]; this package defaults instead to the narrowest sufficient mandate, which leaves a residue with no holder. The subscription-activated candidate declared this gap against itself and routed it; the capability-differentiated candidate carried the same hole silently. The company/human review states the disposition in its own words: the resolution is a staffing decision and belongs to the founder.

packet.decision_required: Name the standing human role that holds custody of a harm or duty when no mandate covers it, and state its consequence ceiling, its alternate and its expiry. Or decide that no fourth tier exists and that the designated maintenance/discovery custodian is terminal.
packet.why_this_owner: It is a staffing decision and a delegation of authority — the company/human review's own words: the resolution is a staffing decision and belongs to the founder. DIRECTIVE §3: risk tolerance and information only the founder holds.
packet.latest_responsible_time: Before the first admitted work order in a class whose harm no existing mandate covers. It does not block the amendment or the builder: the ordered custody resolver is specified with its terminal slot marked unfilled.
options: (a) Name a person with a consequence ceiling, an alternate and an expiry
(b) Engage a professional or service as the terminal element
(c) Delete the fourth tier and make the designated maintenance/discovery custodian terminal
(d) Declare the founder the terminal element, as an explicit exception
consequences: (a) and (b) cost money and a real acceptance act by a party who is not the founder
(c) puts legal-class harm on a custodian whose mandate does not cover it, which is the gap the capability-differentiated candidate carried silently
(d) is honest and makes every unowned harm an interrupt on one person
packet.uncertainty: Whether a harm class with no covering mandate actually arises at these ventures' scale is unmeasured, and it is downstream of the arrival rate of genuinely novel work, which nobody has counted (U-1, the cheapest measurement in the round).
packet.reversibility: High as software, low as a relationship. Naming a party is reversible; telling an outside party who to contact is not.
packet.recommendation: (d) now, (a) or (b) before the first venture carries an outward obligation. The exception is honest, costs nothing, and makes the load visible. Pretending a role exists is the failure mode this packet exists to prevent.
packet.if_no_answer: Admission stops in every class whose harm no existing mandate covers. That is a visible, recorded narrowing, not a silent gap.

question: May anything halt or reverse a capacity shed in the moment, and who decides when a protected-lane holder refuses?

consequences: (a) is fast and auditable and cannot notice that this particular shed is catastrophic, which the workflow-first candidate concedes in its own words

question: What is the size of each reserved lane, its stated minimum and its lapse point?
evidence: The session window resets on schedule whether consumed or not [R8 §3], so a reserve under a non-rolling allowance is waste rather than thrift — the one correct costing of a reservation anywhere in the round. No published denominator exists, so every figure this round can produce is a ratio between arms, and "this design consumes 40% of the allowance" is not a sentence anyone here can write [R8 W-6, MG-03].

packet.decision_required: Per lane: its share of the observed allowance, its stated minimum, and the point before the reset window at which unconsumed reservation releases to the pool.
packet.why_this_owner: These decide what the company gives up under pressure, which is its meaning rather than an engineering parameter. DIRECTIVE §3: risk tolerance.
packet.latest_responsible_time: Before the first shed negotiation. NOT URGENT, for the same reason as the shed-authority packet: no shed can occur at the current concurrency pin, and the cheaper prerequisite is reading the account entitlement (R-G04).
options: Any set of shares. The design fixes only the structure: shares are expressed as FRACTIONS of the observed allowance and never as absolute quantities, because no published denominator exists
The protected due-service and grievance reserves may never be shed, whatever the shares are
The lapse point is time-triggered and independent of any holder's consent, whatever its value
consequences: Generous reserves are destroyed unconsumed at the reset — a reserve under a non-rolling allowance is waste, not thrift
Tight reserves breach minimums under pressure, and the breach is what the founder is alerted to
There is no setting that avoids both, which is why the structure rather than the numbers is what the design fixes
packet.uncertainty: Total. The quantity that would make this arithmetic is the one the provider stopped publishing, so only ratios between arms are computable.
packet.reversibility: High. Shares are data.
packet.recommendation: Adopt 07-integrations-capacity.md §6's existing class shares unchanged as the starting values, set the lapse point at 20% of the window remaining, and treat both as measurements to revise rather than as decisions. The structure is what matters; the numbers are placeholders and must be labelled as such.
packet.if_no_answer: No shed negotiation can run. Since none can occur at the current pin, nothing happens.

question: Is the one-concurrent-native-job pin a provider constraint or a self-imposed policy — what does the account entitlement say?
status: Open; founder owns the read — not yet performed

packet.latest_responsible_time: Before any CapacityPlan revision that raises the concurrency pin, and before F-2 is claimed as exercised. It is the first of the three capacity packets to answer, because Q-020 and Q-021 both defer to it by name.
options: (a) Read the entitlement now and record the observed limit with its source and date
(b) Defer the read to an authenticated custodian, and carry the pin as unknown until one exists
